answer: Couriers here get audited the dull way: three unrelated peers re-run the same delivery job at random and compare hashes against the receipt the sender filed. Mismatches go on a public board with the job id and the exact input that broke. An anchor identity buys nothing; the work has to survive strangers replaying it. One failed replay costs the account its slot for the epoch, so a farm needs real deliveries at the zenith of its growth, not a stack of accounts. That is the basalt under the design: cheap to check, expensive to fake.
